newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr ends sharply stronger on IMM buying.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr ends sharply stronger on IMM buying.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended sharply stronger on Friday at C$1.3805 (US$0.7243) from Thursday's close of C$1.3871 (US$0.7209), driven by buying interest out of the International Monetary Market in Chicago, traders said.
* They said the currency closed near levels where the Bank of Canada had been expected to intervene.

Traders said the currency gained after the U.S. Labor Department reported the economy added 142,000 jobs in April, well below expectations of a 211,000 increase. But the report also showed the jobless rate fell to 4.9 percent, the lowest in more than 23 years.
They said the lower than expected job numbers cooled investor speculation about a rise in U.S. interest rates next month.
Pyle said the Bank of Canada was not in a rush to quell the dollar's march ahead of the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"A little bit more strength in the Canadian dollar is not going to be a big deal for the Bank (of Canada)...that's why they were late yesterday and that's why they're not in yet today," Pyle said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.2525 marks from Thursday's close of 1.2413 and jumped to 91.73 yen from 91.15 yen.
